strengths: Clear and well-motivated core insight: gradient row-space is contained in activation column-space, with convincing empirical evidence (Figure 1) and elegant mathematical formulation (Eq. 9)
Rigorous theoretical framework with subspace-smoothing interpretation (Prop. 5.1-5.2), closed-form expected cosine similarity (Theorem 5.4), and formal conditions for AGZO superiority (Theorem 5.7)
Strong empirical validation of theory: Figure 2 directly confirms gradient alignment predictions; consistent improvements across 8+ tasks on two model scales (Qwen3-0.6B, Pangu-1B)
Practical memory efficiency: maintains forward-only ZO computation model with O(din·r) per-layer overhead and K=3 lightweight power iterations; memory profiling demonstrates negligible overhead
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including cross-platform validation (GPU and NPU), diverse benchmark coverage (SuperGLUE), and careful memory scaling analysis (Figures 3-4)
Well-executed presentation with clear motivation, appropriate mathematical depth, and detailed proofs in appendix
weaknesses: Strong but incompletely validated theoretical assumptions: Theorem 5.7's activation spectral concentration condition (Eq. 33) is indirect and lacks systematic empirical verification across tasks/layers; no analysis of failure modes when assumptions break

Modest empirical improvements: ~2% average gains over MeZO (Qwen3: 0.877 vs 0.858, Pangu: 0.720 vs 0.706), and 3-5% gap to first-order fine-tuning remains substantial, limiting practical significance

Incomplete ablation studies: rank fixed at r=1 without justification or sensitivity analysis; power iteration steps fixed at K=3 without convergence analysis; no study of subspace extraction method alternatives; missing impact analysis for activation aggregation strategy

Limited experimental scope: primarily SuperGLUE classification tasks (missing generation, code, domain-specific tasks); only MeZO and LOZO baselines (missing other ZO variants or FO parameter-efficient methods); only two models in 600M-1B range tested; no training speed comparisons

Reproducibility concerns: no code availability mentioned; implementation details sparse (H_ℓ flattening procedure, sequence boundary handling, power iteration initialization); hyperparameter grid details incomplete; 100× difference in ZO_EPS between Qwen3 and Pangu (1e-2 vs 1e-4) unexplained

Presentation issues: Figure 1 appears duplicated (pages 3-4 and 4-5); memory overhead asserted as 'negligible' without quantification; heavy notation in Section 3.1; generic impact statement adds minimal value
